A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with the same title, author, OSMD-G framework, and headline regret rate. All 19 pages of v1 and 24 pages of v3, including their appendices, support comparison; rendering resolved extraction gaps in mathematical symbols.

before.justification: v1 reports theoretical bounds, mathematical constructions, and algorithm analyses. Table 1 summarizes analytic rates; neither the main text nor Appendices A–D report original empirical outcomes.

after.justification: v3 remains theoretical, including its new counterexample and expanded proofs. Neither the main text nor Appendices A–F report experiments, simulations, or data-analysis outcomes.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 replaces direct importance-weighted rewards with one minus an importance-weighted estimate of 1-r and adds an S=1 centering branch. This substantively revises the update procedure. Mirror descent, truncation, and negatively correlated swap rounding remain.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or conducts task evaluations. The stochastic hard instances and graph constructions are theoretical devices, not newly evaluated scenarios.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates an empirical comparator set. The new comparison with mean-only OSMD is a theoretical counterexample, assessed under T1 and C1.

E3.justification: No experimental protocols, splits, metrics, or evaluation budgets are reported in either version. Changes to theoretical horizon assumptions and algorithm parameter prescriptions are covered under T1 and D1.

E4.justification: Neither version contains empirical ablations, robustness tests, or error analyses. The added impossibility argument is a mathematical result rather than an experimental ablation.

E5.justification: The arm-elimination confidence threshold and Lemma 7 concentration statement are retained across appendix relocation. Neither version reports repeated runs, empirical uncertainty intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: No empirical scores or measured findings are added or revised. Table 1 retains the same three asymptotic regret rates; new and revised theoretical guarantees are assessed under T1.

T1.justification: The lower-bound proof replaces the shared parameter u in [n] with independent coordinates in [n]^S and introduces stopping times; its horizon condition becomes T≥max{S,α³/S}. V3 adds Theorem 3.2 on mean-only OSMD, revises the upper-bound analysis for strongly observable graphs, and adds the S=1 proof in Appendix C. Theorem 1.2 also newly states the lower bound for any decision subset. Theorem 4.1 formalizes the partition example already present in v1 Section 4.1.

C1.justification: The headline minimax rate remains, but the abstract and introduction add the substantive claim that mean matching alone cannot guarantee near-optimal graph-feedback regret. Theorem 1.2 also broadens the reported lower-bound scope from the full action set to any action subset, while adding the T≥S requirement.

C2.justification: V3 explicitly distinguishes insufficiency of mean matching from necessity of negative correlations. Remark 1 explains why loopless nodes are easier to handle when S≥2, and Section 4.3 adds small-horizon and problem-dependent-bound open questions. The existing subset, matroid, and weak-observability discussions largely remain.

D1.justification: Theorem 3.1 revises the explicit learning-rate prescription while retaining ε=1/(KT). Algorithm 3 supplies the missing observation-count operand in its minimum-count update. No code/data access instructions or hardware specifications are added.

R1.justification: V3 adds CHK17, IHS+19, LKLS18, CTMSP+15, and ZvdHCBN23. It updates the discussion of full-bandit tight bounds, attributes the stopping-time proof approach, and adds contextual and problem-dependent connections. The overall research positioning remains.

P1.justification: Section 2 changes from a full proof to an explanatory sketch, with the replacement proof in Appendix A. The upper-bound exposition is reorganized, Section 3.3 is introduced, and Section 4 is reframed around extensions and open problems. Explanations are expanded, appendices reorganized, and the Impact Statement removed.

P2.justification: Algorithm 1 is enlarged and reformatted to display the revised estimator and conditional branch. Algorithms 2 and 3 move with the appendix reorganization. Table 1 and the single-column visual style remain essentially unchanged; neither version contains figures.

improvement.justification: V3 adds useful explanations, a mean-only OSMD counterexample, and a replacement for the lower-bound proof whose flaw it acknowledges. However, unlike v1's full-set statement, Theorem 1.2 asserts a positive lower bound for every action subset: a singleton subset has zero regret under Equation 1, and Appendix A does not justify this extension. This new error in a central guarantee makes the net quality effect of the theoretical additions uncertain.
